summary.headline: Laxmi Dental Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13.9% y-o-y to about INR75 crore, a record, with EBITDA margin at 19.2% and PAT up 23.8%.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue, with consolidated revenue from operations of INR74.7 crore against INR65.6 crore a year earlier. Gross margin was 78.6% and EBITDA rose 20.6% y-o-y to INR14.4 crore at a 19.2% margin, helped by favourable mix and a scanner trading contribution. Dental lab grew 23.5% y-o-y, with international up 37.4%, while aligners grew 28.6%. Management flagged a new US CEO hire, a planned Palghar land purchase to replace rented facilities, and FY27 scanner deployment of 800 to 1,000 units. The company remains debt-free.

segments.name: Dental lab
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 23.5% y-o-y across domestic and international. Domestic lab excluding scanners grew about 12% y-o-y in Q1, per the analyst's question and management's confirmation.

segments.name: International (within dental lab)
segments.commentary: Grew 37.4% y-o-y. CFO said USD moved from about INR85 to INR95, roughly 12% y-o-y currency tailwind, so constant-currency growth is lower but still strong.

segments.name: Aligner solutions
segments.commentary: Grew 28.6% y-o-y. Bizdent grew 27.8% and Vedia grew 29.3%. Management linked growth to the iScope at-home monitoring launch and dentist education.

segments.name: Kids-e-Dental (paediatric)
segments.commentary: Grew 54.4% y-o-y in the quarter. The company holds 60% of its PAT in its adjusted EBITDA calculation.

segments.name: Scanners (trading)
segments.commentary: Sold at about INR3 lakh average to dentists with a trading margin of about 15% to 20%. Scanner mix causes quarter-to-quarter margin swings.

guidance_outlook: Aspiration: 15% to 20% revenue growth and 18% to 20% EBITDA margin. Management said it expects to be in that range, after FY26 margins of about 15.6%.
Domestic lab growth expected to accelerate in Q2, Q3 and Q4 FY27 as satellite labs and scanner-linked customers mature.
Scanner deployment of 800 to 1,000 units targeted for FY27, with the company saying it is on track.
AI-led automation costs are elevated this year and expected to fall next year as scale rises.
Margin expected to be maintained or improved through the year; gross margin should stay stable excluding scanner mix effects.
capex_capacity: Planned FY27 investment in new machinery to modernise and expand manufacturing capacity; no amount disclosed.

Letter of intent executed to acquire land in Palghar, Maharashtra, to replace two rented domestic facilities (Illusion Dental Lab and aligners). Rent is about INR2 crore a year; management said a 3x-size owned facility could otherwise cost INR5 to 6 crore in rent.
No disruption to revenue or productivity expected during the transition, which will be phased. Management cited a 2020 export-unit move from Kandivali to Boisar as precedent.
Aligner capacity utilisation about 70%, with reasonable headroom. Lab utilisation is at a constant 90% to 95% because of custom work.
Digital penetration in domestic network about 75% to 80% (dental lab and aligner combined); international is mostly digital.
demand_pricing: Domestic lab growth slowed to about 12% y-o-y ex-scanners, which management attributed to scanner-led adoption maturing with a 6-month to 18-month gestation period.
Scanner penetration in the industry estimated at about 7% to 8%, with management saying the adoption curve (J-curve) has not yet clearly started.
Management said competition in aligners persists but declined to detail it, citing counter-strategies such as cross-selling.
Aligners are sold only through dentists, not B2C. Management targets general dentists and orthodontists alike.
Branding push includes a brand ambassador, in-clinic branding and social media. Management described itself as the only branded player in crowns.

qa_highlights.question: What differentiates Laxmi Dental products for dentists after the iScan Pro scanner, given no exclusive tie-ups?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 36 years of trust, global quality standards and ISO-certified systems, and innovation, and said it is the only branded crown player.

qa_highlights.question: What is scanner gross margin and how lumpy will margins be?
qa_highlights.answer: Scanners are a trading item with a 15% to 20% margin. Excluding scanners, margins are stable and rising; Q1 margin was 19.2% vs about 15% in the previous quarter and 18% a year ago.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity and utilisation for lab and aligners?
qa_highlights.answer: Aligners at about 70% utilisation. Lab runs at a constant 90% to 95% because of custom work.

qa_highlights.question: Why acquire Palghar land and will there be disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: Goal is to move from two rented sites to one owned facility to cut about INR2 crore rent and gain room to expand. Management expects no revenue disruption.

qa_highlights.question: Why is domestic lab growing only about 12% and when will it improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was 12% y-o-y, attributed to satellite labs adding customer proximity, and expects faster growth from Q2 onwards.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the international growth is currency?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the USD moved from about INR85 to INR95, roughly 12% y-o-y, with the rest from existing DSO and retail business. Management expects the tailwind to persist for some quarters but is unsure beyond that.

qa_highlights.question: Scanner deployment and FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 800 to 1,000 scanner deployments in FY27 and an 18% to 20% margin aspiration; it said Q1 margin supports that range.

risks_watch: Scanner mix drives quarterly gross margin swings; a strong scanner quarter dilutes margin.
Domestic lab growth at about 12% ex-scanners is below the company's 15% to 20% aspiration; Q2 to Q4 acceleration is unproven.
FX tailwind on international growth (USD from about INR85 to INR95) may reverse.
AI-led automation and ECL provisions raised other expenses to INR15.9 crore; cost pressure may persist this year.
Palghar land and facility transition: timing, capex size and rent savings not yet quantified.
Aligner competition, which management declined to detail.
Share price weakness after results drew analyst and retail investor questions; management had no explanation.
